title: GSPC measurement card
description: A single signed measurement result. The envelope carries the signature; `body` is the only part that is signed, and `id` is the SHA-256 of the body's canonical preimage. Schema validity is necessary but NOT sufficient: a schema-valid card can still be a forgery. Run the verifier.

id.description: sha256(preimage).hexdigest(), where preimage is the canonicalised body. Also the card's permanent identifier: it cannot be reassigned without changing the bytes.

pubkey.description: Raw Ed25519 public key. A verifier MUST compare this against a key it obtained independently. Verifying against the key the card carries proves only self-consistency.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature over the preimage bytes.

preimage_rule.description: How the preimage bytes were produced. A verifier that does not implement the stated rule MUST stop and report that it could not check the card, rather than canonicalising on a best-effort basis.

axis.description: The governance axis measured. Names are published alongside the board; this schema does not enumerate them, because the axis set changes by ruling and a frozen list here would silently invalidate future cards.

model.description: Identifier of the system that was measured.

accuracy.description: Proportion of items graded correct on this axis. A FLOAT: an integral value was serialised as `0.0` in the signed preimage, not `0`. See the canonicalisation note in the README.

status.description: `unmeasured` is a first-class published value, not an absence. A cell with no measurement is published as unmeasured rather than omitted, imputed, or left to be read as zero.

issuer.description: The legal person accountable for the measurement.

prev.description: The id of the preceding card, or a genesis marker. This is the only structural defence against a silently truncated published set: the index is not signed, but `prev` is inside the signed body.

public_framing.description: How the issuer described the board's coverage at the time of signing. Historical: it is fixed at signing time and does not track later rulings.

verify.description: A convenience pointer to published verification instructions. NOT required to verify: verification is offline and needs no service.
